hook: Ilya Sutskever was born in Nizhny Novgorod, Russia, and moved with his family first to Israel and then to Canada, where he studied computer science at the University of Toronto under Geoffrey Hinton. In 2012 he co-authored the AlexNet paper with Alex Krizhevsky and Hinton, a deep convolutional network that sharply cut ImageNet classification error rates and helped launch the modern deep learning era. He followed this in 2014 with Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks, showing that a general encoder-decoder architecture could handle tasks like machine translation. In December 2015 he co-founded OpenAI, serving first as Research Director and later as Chief Scientist while the lab built its GPT model series. He left OpenAI in 2024 and co-founded Safe Superintelligence Inc with Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy, a company dedicated to a single goal, building safe superintelligence, and became its CEO in mid-2025 after Gross departed.

standing.watch: What remains unresolved in the records is the litigation itself: every listed case is marked as filed with docket monitoring active and no development recorded yet by this tracker, so no outcome, ruling or settlement appears. The records also leave open the course of Safe Superintelligence Inc under Sutskever as CEO following the departure of Daniel Gross, with no funding, valuation or product milestone recorded. No planned listing or additional dispute involving Sutskever appears in the records. Where the records are thin, they say only this much.
standing.record: The site's records tie Sutskever to OpenAI as a founded company and list a series of lawsuits naming OpenAI entities, including USA Today Co., Inc. v. OpenAI Foundation, TradeSun, Inc. v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, Bass v. OpenAI, LLC, United States v. OpenAI OpCo LLC, GRANT v. OPENAI INC, Smigelski v. OpenAI OpCo, LLC, and JIANG v. OPENAI GROUP PBC. One listed case, Buist v. Anthropic, PBC, names Anthropic rather than an OpenAI entity. For each of these the tracker records only that the case was filed and that docket monitoring is active, with no development recorded yet. The pattern is a founder whose research and OpenAI history are documented alongside litigation against OpenAI entities that remains at the filing stage. The records do not connect Sutskever personally to any of these cases.
standing.standing: Ilya Sutskever stands as a co-founder and the chief executive of Safe Superintelligence Inc, a company the records describe as dedicated to a single goal of building safe superintelligence. He became its CEO in mid-2025 after co-founder Daniel Gross departed. Before that he co-founded OpenAI in December 2015 and served as Research Director and later Chief Scientist, and he left OpenAI in 2024. His standing also rests on foundational research, including the 2012 AlexNet paper with Alex Krizhevsky and Geoffrey Hinton and the 2014 Sequence to Sequence Learning paper. The records show him leading a company with one stated aim rather than a product line.
